extractor.note: Read every paragraph carrying transcend- (outside transcendental), immanen-, surpass or going beyond, in file order. Strata are set only where the section is the dated text itself (Text Nr. 2 and Supplement I ca. 1920, Text Nr. 3 1921); sections whose text number the record cannot tie to a date carry none. Supplement XXXI carries the theme only in its heading and is not recorded.

coverage_note: Term-led pass over the whole file (lines 1-1463): every paragraph containing the transcendence family, including bare transcendent and immanent, was read; paragraphs without such a word were not read.

units.claim: The background datum is an immanent, originally constituted intentional objectuality that functions for a transcendent apperception in the pregnant sense.
units.quote: It is an "intentional objectuality," an immanent one, originally constituted, here functioning in a certain way for a "transcendent apperception," an apperception in the pregnant sense.

units.claim: Husserl distinguishes immanent constitutions, which play out in pure passivity under rigid lawfulness, from transcendent constitutions, in which ego-activity plays a genetically constitutive role.
units.quote: There is a difference between immanent and transcendent constitutions — between those that originally and genetically must play out in pure passivity and according to original and rigid lawfulness (like the constitution of immanent data) and transcendent constitutions

units.claim: Transcendent objects are always already apperceived and pre-given as background-things, whereas immanent data can in their first genesis be constituted without apperception.
units.quote: Transcendent things are always pre-given in this pregnant sense; immanent data are not.

units.claim: In the immanent sphere prominence and association take place but create nothing new, unlike apperception in thing-constitution.
units.quote: In the immanent sphere, prominence and association indeed take place, but they create nothing new.

units.claim: Since transcendent constitution always involves a universe of practical possibilities organized through kinaestheses, every perception is founded on prior apperceptive perception.
units.quote: since transcendent constitution always involves a universe of practical possibilities, every act of perception is itself founded on prior apperceptive perception

units.claim: Consciousness is not only but is conscious, and its being is immanently constituted being, individually and for the whole stream.
units.quote: Consciousness is not only, but it is conscious; its being is immanently constituted being, individually and for the entire "stream of consciousness."

units.claim: Unlike the world, the immanent time and time-world is not a world for us, not constantly there and at our disposal for immediate access.
units.quote: But the immanent "time" and "time-world" is not a world for us, not constantly there for us in such a way that we could just look toward it, perceive it

units.claim: In the constitutive order the object of nature-time precedes the object of immanent time, and the outer world precedes the stream of experience.
units.quote: In this sense, nature-time, i.e. the object of nature-time, precedes immanent time, i.e. the object of immanent time; the outer world precedes the stream of experience.

units.claim: The immanent sphere can be constituted as existing only from the already constituted objective world, and even then remains not pre-given as the experiential world is.
units.quote: Even after this constitutive achievement, the immanent sphere is and remains not pre-given in the way the objective experiential world is.

units.claim: In immanence there lies no telos for the life of the ego; only the psychologist and epistemologist have an interest in it.
units.quote: In immanence there lies no telos for the life of the ego.

units.claim: No immanent world is constituted because in the course of genesis all immanent acquisition enters into mundane constitution.
units.quote: In genetic originality, immanent affection and grasping are indeed there, but in the course of genesis all immanent acquisition enters into mundane constitution; immanence is absorbed into the function of mundane constitution.

units.claim: Empathy transcends not only the present of consciousness but with it the whole life-past and life-future as co-valid.
units.quote: Empathy transcends not only my consciousness-present but, in one with it, my entire life-past and life-future as co-valid.

units.claim: The intentional analysis of the transcendental own life in its self-transcendence brings to light founding relations among transcending functions, presentification intertwined with the transcendences of mundane perception.
units.quote: The intentional analysis of the transcendental own life in its self-transcendence here brings to light the founding relations of different transcending functions — the functions of presentification intertwined with the transcendences of "mundane perception."

units.claim: Husserl distinguishes presentations and appresentations: every transcendent perception presents its transcendent object only by means of appresentation.
units.quote: Every transcendent perception can present its transcendent object only through the means of appresentation.

units.claim: The theoretical interest in being and truth can transcend situational relativity and pursue the identical in its so-being.
units.quote: But the interest in being and truth can transcend situational relativity: the theoretical interest can station itself above the respective interests and pursue the identical in its so-being consequentially

units.claim: On the possible non-being of the world, Husserl asks whether transcendental constitution could dissolve while the ego of immanence remains.
units.quote: Could the transcendental constitution dissolve while I yet remain as ego of immanence?

absences.expected_because: The primal institution of the sense of pre-given individual being and world is the genesis that Text Nr. 2 divides into immanent constitution and transcendent constitution of pre-given things.
